column1: # What a long Treasury DID across the equity drawdowns of the last 24 years, on the model bond's
# footing: for every equity peak-to-trough decline of 15% or worse, the bond's LOG return over the
# same span, in percent, and the fund's empirical duration over that span. The model's bond is a
# 13.5-year bond (`DURATION_REF`), so each episode is graded as bondPct x 13.5 / duration, and the
# targets `bond growth-crash` and `bond infl-crash` are the MEDIANS of those scaled returns by
# regime -- the duration-relative footing `bond vol % (24y)` is already on. An unscaled TLT number
# grades a 13.5-year bond against a 17-year fund's move. `BondCrashSuite` / `bond_crash_tests`
# re-derive both targets from the rows below.
# THE SAMPLE IS SIX EPISODES and that is the honest limit of this anchor -- the growth median is a
# median of five, and the inflation target is the one 2022 episode. `-noise` prices that in: over
# 24-year histories the model produces growth-crash readings from about +2% to +28%, so one record
# barely pins it, and the target's weight is small for that reason rather than by choice.
# Equity SPY, bond TLT, daily Yahoo adjusted closes over their overlap, 2002-07-30..2026-08-03.
# duration: TLT's empirical duration over the episode, in years -- minus the slope of its weekly
#   (5-session) log return on the weekly change of the 20-year constant-maturity Treasury yield
#   (FRED DGS20), over peak..trough. This is the sensitivity that turned the yield path into
#   bondPct, so it is the like-for-like scale; the fund's published effective duration moved
#   between 15 and 19 over these years (14.89 on 2026-08-22, ishares-2026-08-22.tsv).
# regime: growth or inflation, by whether the decline is the 2022 inflation shock -- the model
#   splits on its own `inflPress` and this is the record's only inflation-regime drawdown.
peak
